title: Keyless Entry / RKE Circuit (B2700-v3)
shortDescription: A keyless / remote keyless entry (RKE) circuit fault stored as B2700-v3.
fullDescription: The body controller logs B2700-v3 when a keyless / remote keyless entry (rke) circuit fault is detected. The fault often disables the affected convenience or safety function until repaired and may persist after a battery reset.
safetyImpact: None directly; doors may not lock or unlock from the fob and panic alarm may be inhibited.

causes.cause: Weak or dead key fob battery
Door latch switch out of adjustment
Damaged wiring at A-pillar or door jamb

symptoms: Key fob does not lock / unlock doors
Panic button does not trigger horn

fixSteps.title: Replace Fob Battery
fixSteps.instruction: Install a fresh CR2032 (or per spec) battery; clear codes and retest from 5 m.

fixSteps.title: Reprogram Fob
fixSteps.instruction: Follow OEM relearn procedure or use a scan tool to add the fob.

fixSteps.title: Test RKE Receiver
fixSteps.instruction: With scan tool monitor RKE receiver data while pressing the fob; signal should register.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check power, ground, and signal lines to the receiver / antenna against schematic.

faq.a: Aftermarket fobs sometimes set this code; OEM is the safe choice.
Cold weather and weak batteries shorten range and trigger intermittent codes.

title: Immobilizer / Anti-Theft Circuit (B2900-v4)
shortDescription: An immobilizer / anti-theft authentication fault stored as B2900-v4.
fullDescription: The body controller logs B2900-v4 when an immobilizer / anti-theft authentication fault is detected. The fault often disables the affected convenience or safety function until repaired and may persist after a battery reset.
safetyImpact: The engine may refuse to start; vehicle may be stranded until reauthenticated.

causes.cause: Failed immobilizer antenna ring at ignition
BCM / IMMO module replaced without coding
Low battery during start causing comm dropout
Wiring fault between IMMO and ECM

symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start
Key light stays on after crank

fixSteps.title: Verify Battery Voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm battery is at least 12.4 V resting; low voltage routinely sets IMMO codes.

fixSteps.title: Try Spare Key
fixSteps.instruction: If the spare starts the car, the original key transponder is faulty.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Antenna Ring
fixSteps.instruction: Check the immobilizer antenna at the ignition lock for breaks or unplugged connector.

fixSteps.title: Perform Key Relearn
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool with security access to relearn keys to the BCM / IMMO module.

faq.a: Not legally or safely; insurance and theft protection rely on it.
EEPROM in the IMMO can corrupt during low-voltage events; key relearn restores it.

title: Lost Communication With Body Module (U0140-v3)
shortDescription: Lost communication with a body / convenience module on the CAN bus stored as U0140-v3.
fullDescription: The network controller logs U0140-v3 when lost communication with a body / convenience module on the can bus is detected. The fault often disables the affected convenience or safety function until repaired and may persist after a battery reset.
safetyImpact: Locks, lighting, wipers, or HVAC controls tied to the missing module may be disabled.

causes.cause: Open or shorted CAN bus wiring

symptoms: Multiple unrelated warning lights on cluster
Wipers or HVAC blower not responding
Module missing in scan tool list

fixSteps.title: Scan All Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Read fault codes from every module to identify which is offline and which still talk.

fixSteps.title: Check Power & Ground
fixSteps.instruction: Verify B+ and ground at the missing module's connector are within spec.

fixSteps.title: Inspect CAN Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Measure 60 ohms across CAN-H / CAN-L with key off and battery disconnected.

fixSteps.title: Replace / Code Module
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM replacement and code it to the vehicle with a dealer-level tool.

faq.q: Can a single bad module take down the bus?
faq.a: Yes; an internally shorted module pulls CAN low and silences the network.

faq.q: Why does it come and go?
faq.a: Connector corrosion or a marginal solder joint in the module is a common cause.

title: Lost Communication With Steering / Seat / Door Module (U0200-v2)
shortDescription: Lost communication with a steering, seat, or door control module stored as U0200-v2.
fullDescription: The network controller logs U0200-v2 when lost communication with a steering, seat, or door control module is detected. The fault often disables the affected convenience or safety function until repaired and may persist after a battery reset.
safetyImpact: Steering wheel buttons, memory seats, or door functions may be disabled.

causes.cause: Broken wiring in door harness boot
Connector corrosion under seat or in door

symptoms: Window / mirror / lock switches inoperative on one door
Memory seat refuses to recall positions

fixSteps.title: Identify Offline Module
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool topology view to confirm exactly which node is silent.

fixSteps.title: Flex-Test Door Boot
fixSteps.instruction: Open and close the affected door while watching live data; broken wires reveal themselves.

fixSteps.title: Repair Harness
fixSteps.instruction: Solder and heat-shrink any broken conductors in the door / seat boot.

fixSteps.title: Replace and Code Module
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM module and program it; perform any required relearns.

faq.a: The flex point of the door boot fatigues the wiring; this is by far the top failure spot.

faq.q: Will resetting the BCM fix it?
faq.a: Only if the wiring and module are healthy; otherwise the code returns immediately.

symptoms: Window / mirror / lock switches inoperative on one door
Memory seat refuses to recall positions

fixSteps.title: Identify Offline Module
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool topology view to confirm exactly which node is silent.

fixSteps.title: Flex-Test Door Boot
fixSteps.instruction: Open and close the affected door while watching live data; broken wires reveal themselves.

fixSteps.title: Repair Harness
fixSteps.instruction: Solder and heat-shrink any broken conductors in the door / seat boot.

fixSteps.title: Replace and Code Module
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM module and program it; perform any required relearns.

faq.a: The flex point of the door boot fatigues the wiring; this is by far the top failure spot.

faq.q: Will resetting the BCM fix it?
faq.a: Only if the wiring and module are healthy; otherwise the code returns immediately.

title: Lost Communication With Steering / Seat / Door Module (U0204)
shortDescription: Lost communication with a steering, seat, or door control module stored as U0204.
fullDescription: The network controller logs U0204 when lost communication with a steering, seat, or door control module is detected. The fault often disables the affected convenience or safety function until repaired and may persist after a battery reset.
safetyImpact: Steering wheel buttons, memory seats, or door functions may be disabled.

title: Instrument Cluster / Mileage Memory Fault (B3500-v2)
shortDescription: An instrument cluster mileage or memory integrity fault stored as B3500-v2.
fullDescription: The body controller logs B3500-v2 when an instrument cluster mileage or memory integrity fault is detected. The fault often disables the affected convenience or safety function until repaired and may persist after a battery reset.
safetyImpact: Odometer or fuel level may read incorrectly; warning lamps may not display correctly.
symptoms: Warning lamps stay on or off incorrectly

fixSteps.title: Verify Charging System
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm 13.8-14.6 V at idle; weak alternators corrupt cluster EEPROMs over time.

fixSteps.title: Read EEPROM Backup
fixSteps.instruction: Some shops can read and rewrite the EEPROM to recover mileage.

fixSteps.title: Update Cluster Firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Apply latest factory cluster software via dealer tool, then clear codes.

fixSteps.title: Replace Cluster
fixSteps.instruction: Fit OEM cluster and program mileage and VIN per OEM procedure.

faq.a: Only to match the original mileage during a legitimate cluster repair / swap; falsifying mileage is illegal.
It must be programmed with your VIN and mileage or the immobilizer will not pair.
